questions.questionText: What ML operation is the dot product directly responsible for?
options: It has no real use in machine learning
The weighted sum computed by every neuron, plus similarity scoring in attention and embeddings
questions.correctAnswer: The weighted sum computed by every neuron, plus similarity scoring in attention and embeddings
questions.explanation: A neuron's weighted sum, cosine similarity for embeddings, and attention's query-key scoring are all built directly on the dot product.

questions.questionText: What does the matrix operation W @ x + b represent in a neural network?
options: Exactly one layer of a neural network: transforming an input vector into the next layer's pre-activation values
Only used for image data, never for numeric features
A method for splitting training and test data
questions.correctAnswer: Exactly one layer of a neural network: transforming an input vector into the next layer's pre-activation values
questions.explanation: W @ x + b is literally the computation a neural network layer performs — the weight matrix transforms the input vector, and the bias vector shifts the result, before an activation function is applied.

questions.questionText: What does cosine similarity measure, in terms of the dot product formula a·b = |a||b|cos(θ)?
options: The exact numeric distance between two vectors
The angle between two vectors, isolated from their magnitudes by dividing out |a| and |b|
The number of dimensions two vectors share
Whether two vectors have identical values
questions.correctAnswer: The angle between two vectors, isolated from their magnitudes by dividing out |a| and |b|
questions.explanation: Normalizing the dot product by both vectors' magnitudes leaves only cos(θ), which is why cosine similarity captures directional similarity independent of vector length.
